This is ONE continuous video, NOT multiple videos, NOT separate clips, NOT separate sequences, and NOT a montage.

All actions below happen consecutively inside the SAME continuous scene.

Preserve Yasuo exactly as shown in the provided reference. Keep the same face, facial structure, hairstyle, hair length, outfit, armor, accessories, katana, body proportions and colors throughout the entire scene.

Preserve the same forest, heavy rain, darkness, atmospheric fog, lighting direction and visual atmosphere from the provided environment reference.

Begin with Yasuo already running at full speed through the dark forest in heavy rain.

Several armed soldiers are chasing him from behind. They remain partially hidden by rain, darkness, trees and fog.

Use a low rear tracking camera following close behind Yasuo.

Yasuo runs naturally with realistic body weight and momentum. His boots strike wet mud and shallow puddles, throwing water backward. His wet hair and clothing react naturally to his movement, wind and rain.

Wet branches and tree trunks occasionally pass through the foreground as the camera follows him.

The soldiers shout from behind:

“He’s ahead!”

“Don’t let him escape!”

Keep Yasuo running continuously.

Without cutting to another scene, smoothly move the camera from behind Yasuo toward his side and then around to the front.

The camera now travels backward while Yasuo continues running toward it.

Yasuo suddenly senses danger behind him.

His expression changes subtly.

While still running, he turns his head slightly toward the threat behind him.

One pursuing soldier fires ONE arrow toward Yasuo.

Only one arrow is fired.

The camera rapidly shifts focus from Yasuo to the incoming arrow.

Show the physical arrow flying through the heavy rain toward him. Rain droplets scatter around it.

Use only a very brief cinematic slow-motion moment as the arrow gets close.

The arrow has no glow, no magical trail and no energy effects.

Immediately return to normal speed.

Yasuo reacts.

He plants one foot firmly into the wet muddy ground.

Because of his running momentum, his boot slides slightly through the mud.

Yasuo rapidly pivots around the planted foot and turns to face the incoming arrow.

Keep the movement grounded and physically believable. His feet remain in contact with the terrain and his body clearly carries the momentum from running.

During the pivot, Yasuo performs one fast, controlled sword motion and generates Wind Wall.

Wind Wall must NOT look like a magical energy shield.

Represent it as an extremely powerful zone of compressed moving air.

The wind itself is almost invisible.

Show its power through the environment:

Heavy rain suddenly bends violently sideways.

Mist is blasted outward.

Wet leaves spiral through the air.

Loose debris is pushed away.

Grass and vegetation flatten under the pressure.

Nearby branches shake violently.

Water is blasted from leaves.

Yasuo’s wet hair and clothing react to the pressure.

A subtle distortion in the moisture-filled air can reveal the compressed wind, but there must be no solid glowing wall.

The incoming arrow reaches the compressed air directly in front of Yasuo.

Clearly show the arrow being violently deflected sideways.

The arrow remains a physical object. It does not explode and does not disappear. Show it spinning away through the rain and leaving the frame.

Yasuo remains firmly on the ground.

The compressed wind quickly dissipates.

The rain returns naturally to its normal downward direction.

As the wind disappears, several pursuing soldiers become visible through the rain and fog behind Yasuo.

They continue running toward him but are still several meters away.

They do NOT attack him yet.

Yasuo uses his remaining momentum to slide across the wet muddy ground.

Mud and rainwater spray around his boots.

Move the camera into a dramatic low-angle medium close-up as Yasuo finishes the slide and stops.

Heavy rain continues falling around him.

Yasuo slowly raises himself into a stable combat-ready position.

His breathing is heavy but controlled.

His expression is calm, focused and serious.

The soldiers continue approaching through the foggy forest in the background.

Yasuo moves one hand toward the handle of his katana.

Move slightly closer as his hand firmly grips the katana handle.

He does NOT draw the sword.

End the scene at this exact moment:

Yasuo is stopped in the heavy rain, facing the approaching threat, one hand firmly gripping the handle of his still-sheathed katana while several soldiers approach through the rain and fog behind him.

Do not continue into the sword fight.

Use only brief slow motion for the arrow.

Use controlled handheld movement.

Keep all action visually readable.

Use a wider composition when the arrow reaches Wind Wall so Yasuo, the arrow and the physical effect of the wind can be clearly understood in the same moment.

Finish with a dramatic low-angle medium close-up.

Avoid random cuts, excessive camera shaking and unnecessary camera movement.
